headline: Clinton order kept certain existing federal advisory committees running instead of letting them expire.
what_it_does: This order extended the life of a set of federal advisory committees, which are groups that give advice to the President and federal agencies. Without action, such committees can end after a set time. Orders like this usually extend committees for about two years. The title does not say which committees were covered.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the covered federal advisory committees
who_it_affects.how: They could keep serving and advising the government because their committees did not expire.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that rely on these committees
who_it_affects.how: They kept getting advice from these committees without having to set up new ones.
